summary: Full end-to-end testing of Invoice/Pay app. All 14 backend pytest tests passed (root, paypal config, CRUD, mark-paid, paypal 503 when unconfigured, totals math). Frontend Playwright e2e covered dashboard header (CORY BURNETT + 'or Overflow Investment Legacy'), title-font-larger-than-subtitle assertion, navigation to /invoices/new, form input, live totals computation, save -> /pay/:id navigation, pay page rendering (totals, customer, large header at 128px), PayPal-not-configured warning banner, copy pay link to clipboard, edit nav, delete with confirm, and stats card updates. No failures.
critical_code_review_comments: PayPal capture endpoint (/api/invoices/{id}/paypal/capture/{order_id}) is publicly callable - any caller could potentially mark an invoice paid by guessing order IDs. Recommend validating the order_id belongs to invoice.paypal_order_id stored from create-order, and verify capture status from PayPal response before marking paid.
CORS allow_origins defaults to '*' with allow_credentials=True - browsers reject this combination. For production, set explicit origins in CORS_ORIGINS env.
Invoice numbers are not enforced unique at the DB level - duplicate invoice_number values are allowed. Consider a unique index if business-critical.
No authentication on invoice CRUD - anyone with the URL can create/edit/delete invoices. Acceptable for MVP but flag for production.
seed_data_creation: Test invoices created and cleaned up within tests (TEST_ prefix). One invoice created via Playwright and deleted at end of run.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend tests live in /app/backend/tests/test_invoices.py. PayPal SECRET is intentionally empty -> /config/paypal returns configured=false and create-order returns 503; UI shows amber 'PayPal not configured' banner. When PayPal creds are added later, retest the create-order/capture flow in sandbox.
